comments.body: Landed as Gerrit change 3106, commit 1f452719aa7 (LLM-Review +1 with no advisories, Verified +1, 0 unresolved). Reproduced first with real keys before any change: a certificate signed under a pinned key marked revoked verified as certified with trust_basis pinned_environment in advisory mode AND under verify.require_environment, so revocation was ignored even when the gate restricts trust to pinned keys. Cause: d909 added the revoked-key filter for the own principal only. Fix: _opcert_trust_root now passes unrevoked_only=True for every principal. 2 of the 3 new tests fail on the old code (advisory mode reported pinned_environment; enforcement certified); the forged-payload control and an unrevoked pinned key behave as before. 41 tests in the three opcert files and 739 opcert/attestation tests pass. make verify locally: only the 17 known pandoc failures, no errors; Linux CI green. Limits: no key-era check, so a certificate signed BEFORE the key's revocation is also refused under enforcement (fails closed, same rule the operator chose for the own principal in d909); in advisory mode, the project default, such a certificate still verifies on its embedded key like any unpinned one (c21f design). Enforcement is not enabled in this project today, so live impact was low.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
Found while investigating bug d909-5158-adab-4fe7 (2026-10-24, code reading only; not reproduced). In `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`, the foreign-principal path of `_opcert_trust_root` uses `_pinned_environment_keys`, which returns every keyring entry with a public key, including entries whose `revoked_at_log_position` is set. `verify_opcert_record` has no tickets-log position for the certificate, so it cannot apply the era checks (`added_at_log_position` / `revoked_at_log_position`, verdict `key_not_valid_at_era`) that `verify_required_environment` applies.

## Reproduction (2026-10-25, current main, real keys)
A certificate signed by environment A's key, with A pinned in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` and that key marked revoked (`revoked_at_log_position` set), verified by environment B through `signing.verify_signature`:
- advisory mode (the project default): `verdict certified`, `trust_basis pinned_environment`.
- with `verify.require_environment` and `verify.opcert_enforce_since` set to A: still `certified`, `trust_basis pinned_environment`, `verified True`.
So the revocation field is ignored on the foreign-principal path, including under enforcement. The hypothesis in the observation above is confirmed.

## Root cause
`_opcert_trust_root` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`) calls `_pinned_environment_keys(principal, repo_root, unrevoked_only=is_own)`, and `is_own` is false for a foreign principal, so every pinned key is trusted, revoked ones included (d909 added the filter for the own principal only and deferred this path to this ticket). `verify_opcert_record` has no tickets-log position for the certificate, so it cannot apply the era checks that `verify_required_environment` applies.

## Decision carried over
The operator chose, for the own principal in d909, to trust pinned unrevoked keys with no era check. This ticket applies the same rule to the foreign-principal path. It fails closed: a certificate signed before a key's revocation by that now-revoked key is no longer labelled as pinned trust; under enforcement it is refused (`foreign_key`), in advisory mode it still verifies on its embedded key like any unpinned key (c21f design). Threading the certificate's log position through for era validity stays out of scope.

## Approach
1. In `_opcert_trust_root`, always call `_pinned_environment_keys(..., unrevoked_only=True)`, for the own and the foreign principal alike. Remove the `unrevoked_only` parameter's default of False from the only caller that relied on it; keep the parameter for `_rotated_own_key_verdict`.
2. Update the comment at that call site, which currently says the foreign path is deliberately revoked-inclusive.

## Scope
In scope: `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py` (or a new sibling module). Out of scope: era validity of pinned keys and `verify_required_environment`.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py tests/unit/test_opcert_own_principal_rotation_d909.py tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py -q
make verify
```
New tests with real keys: a foreign certificate under a pinned, revoked key is refused (`foreign_key`) under enforcement and labelled `envelope_key`, not `pinned_environment`, in advisory mode; a foreign certificate under a pinned unrevoked key still verifies as `pinned_environment`; a forged payload under a pinned revoked key still fails. Failure case: the first two fail on main (`certified`, `pinned_environment`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A foreign-principal certificate under a pinned, revoked key is refused under `verify.require_environment` and never labelled `pinned_environment` (checked: new tests, which fail on main with `certified`).
- [x] A foreign-principal certificate under a pinned, unrevoked key still verifies with `trust_basis` `pinned_environment` (checked: existing `test_pinned_environment_key_is_the_trust_basis_when_available`).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).
